Comic and podcaster Duncan Trussell returns to the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1666. Trussell, host of his own family-hour style show, is famous for long, funny talks that slide from jokes into deep questions. With Rogan, an old friend, the chat runs free and unplanned.

The two riff on love, death, faith, and the strange shape of the universe. Trussell mixes stand-up bits with real feeling about loss and wonder. Rogan plays the straight man, grounding the flights of fancy with plain questions. Fans of either man get the warm, weird hangout both shows are known for.
podcast-tuckercarlson-5V6jljDrjOU:
Singer Aaron Lewis tells Tucker Carlson that country music filled his whole childhood. He grew up in northern New England, in deep woods country. His grandparents' home in Vermont was a safe place in hard years.

Lewis fronted the rock band Staind before turning to country songs. The title charges that radio blacklisted him for his views. He also claims labels push weak music on purpose to shape culture. Carlson draws out tales of fame and fallout. The episode mixes memoir with a grievance the music business rarely airs. His voice stays raw and unpolished throughout.
podcast-tuckercarlson-SVcSqvBKAOU:
Tucker Carlson asks why House Speaker Mike Johnson keeps doing the left's bidding. Johnson rose as a quiet conservative from Louisiana. His deals with rivals soon angered his own base.

Carlson charges that the speaker funds and backs rival priorities. He calls the pattern a betrayal of voters who won the House. The episode asks if one party truly rules Washington. No guest shares the hour; the host builds the case alone. It is a sharp lament from the right, aimed at a leader its own side chose. The charge comes from inside his own camp.
